chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Segregated dances in Jackson
summary: Ellington and Lunceford played only white dances in Jackson; at Black dances whites sat in roped-off seating.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, Jimmie Lunceford I wanted to hear. But Jimmie Lunceford and Duke Ellington, the whole time I was at home and could go and hear bands, they never played for the Black dances. Maybe they couldn't afford them or something...
They came through, yeah, but they would play for White dances, you know. During those days it was highly segregated. Like, if it was a band that the White people
wanted to hear, they would have a little section of seats roped off for them, where they could come to the Black dances and hear the music anyway.

Oh yeah. But they had a section, a special section for them, where they had these bench-like seats, you know, almost like a stadium type seat -- and they would sit in that section and hear the band. You know, they couldn't come down and dance, but they could sit up there and hear the band.
